_note: How much research each run does. Research runs every 15 minutes and starts as many researchers as the queue needs, up to sweep.researchers (the cap on usage); an empty queue starts none. Gap searchers: sweep.gap_workers every sweep.gap_every_minutes (by the usage ledger's clock, which survives a restart of the loop; the interval doubles with every four gap runs in a row that added nothing, up to sweep.gap_max_every_minutes, and one run that adds an event brings it back: scripts/lib/gates.mjs gapEveryMinutes), plus sweep.gap_spare_workers while the 5-hour usage window is under sweep.gap_spare_below_pct of its estimate, none when usage is tight (measured 2026-11-19/20: 122 gap runs added 11 events, 91% added nothing, $3.58 per event against $0.95 for a researcher). The backlog desk only acts when more than backlog.leave_for_sweep stories are waiting. The editor job may move these by at most a quarter a week; the owner can set them to anything. headless true (owner, 2026-11-19): every AI job runs as one scripts/run-job.mjs call in swarm phases (plan, claim leases, work, check, retry, commit, report); a job whose workers cannot read the web here falls back to subagents. sweep.review_workers: every research run also starts up to this many reviewers (continuous second review), each with up to review.events_per_reviewer events; with two or more, reviewer 1 takes the events that started waiting most recently (so an event published in one cycle is reviewed in the next) and the others the oldest first, and reviewers start alternating with researchers instead of after them (scripts/review.mjs planBatches, scripts/run-job.mjs mixWork). Raised from 2 to 4 on 2026-11-20: published -> second review was p50 36 min, p90 1099 min against the 15-minute target. The review desk catches the rest. flow: research is one continuous loop (run-job.mjs flow): collect, research new stories and review earlier events in parallel, commit, repeat every min_cycle_minutes or as soon as a cycle ends; it lives `minutes` and the research schedules restart it. flow.update_workers: each cycle also starts up to this many updaters on published events with new reporting (scripts/updates.mjs); flow.followup_every_minutes: how often the loop also runs the follow-up desk on developing and claimed events (by the usage ledger's clock, not the process's: until 2026-11-23 it ran at every restart of the loop, every 15 minutes; which events it takes: followup_desk). flow.grid_workers / flow.grid_per_worker: each cycle also runs scripts/grid.mjs collect, then starts up to grid_workers grid researchers (role grid) on the biggest grid outages that need a cause, grid_per_worker incidents each (scripts/grid-desk.mjs plan and apply; 0 turns it off). flow.outage_workers / flow.outage_per_worker: each cycle also starts up to outage_workers outage checkers (role outage) on unchecked outage reports (news-reported power outages, IODA internet disruptions, status-page outages), outage_per_worker each (scripts/outage-desk.mjs plan and apply; 0 turns it off; off when usage is tight or stopped). outage_desk: the desk's thresholds (see its own _note). flow.idle_backoff_minutes: how long the loop waits after 0, 1, 2+ idle cycles in a row; collection keeps min_cycle_minutes during a longer wait and work found starts the next cycle at once. usage_budget: see its own _note (scripts/lib/usage.mjs). Owner, 2026-11-21 ("use whatever it needs"; accuracy first): sweep.researchers 6 -> 8, sweep.review_workers 4 -> 6 and max_parallel 6 -> 8; the code caps are 16 researchers, 8 reviewers and 12 in parallel. Which researcher, updater and follow-up batches run on Opus is a rule in scripts/lib/routing.mjs (config/models.json _note). flow.claims_workers / flow.claims_per_worker: each cycle also starts up to claims_workers claims checkers (role claims) on ransomware and extortion leak-site claims, most notable victim first, claims_per_worker each (scripts/claims-desk.mjs plan and apply; 0 turns it off; on in every usage level except stop). claims_desk: the desk's windows (see its own _note). usage_budget: see its own _note (scripts/lib/usage.mjs). flow.foreground_minutes (default 7): the dispatcher runs the loop in the FOREGROUND for this many minutes per sweep wake, not as one ~100-minute background process. A cloud session reaps a backgrounded process a few minutes after the turn ends, so the long loop died before its researchers finished or committed (it looked alive by heartbeat while publishing nothing); a short foreground run finishes its cycles and commits before the turn ends, the frequent sweep schedules give continuous coverage, and FLOW_LOCK still makes a second session stand by. Kept under the 10-minute foreground tool cap; set it higher only on a host that is not a cloud session. headless_foreground_minutes (default 8): every other headless job (backlog, review, analyst, deep-sweep and the quick ones) is dispatched in the FOREGROUND for at most this long, for the same reason — run-job.mjs runs a worker pool (triagers, researchers, reviewers) that takes several minutes, and a backgrounded run is reaped by the cloud session before the workers finish (seen as backlog committing '0 new' after only its planning step). A foreground run finishes and commits before the turn ends; a job that ever needs longer is cut and the next scheduled run commits the leftover with finish.mjs --force. Also under the 10-minute tool cap.

followup_desk._note: The follow-up desk's planner (scripts/followup-desk.mjs, the gate in scripts/lib/gates.mjs followupGate; owner, 2026-11-23). Every flow.followup_every_minutes a script decides which events get a follow-up worker; no due event, no worker. Pool: events of the last window_days that are developing, claimed, single-source, carry a date_note or are severity 3. An event is planned when a lead that matches it from a page it does not cite is newer than its last follow-up (something new to read), or when nobody has updated or followed it up for base_hours, doubling with every follow-up in a row that changed nothing (6, 12, 24, 48 h ...), never more than max_hours; severity 3, exploited and developing events never wait longer than urgent_max_hours. An event that is in the pool only for its severity (a settled advisory) waits sev3_quiet_hours for its first follow-up. Everything else is skipped with its reason and the time it is due next (the plan line, status.json followup_note, efficiency.json gates). workers x per_worker: how many events one run of the desk hands out (3 x 2 every 2 hours = 72 looks a day; the desk was designed for 5 every 2 hours = 60, and ran 5 every 15 minutes by mistake on 22 November), in batches of per_worker (a short run re-reads far less context than one long one; config/models.json caps followup and followup-deep to match: about 9 turns an event). Severity 3 and exploited events go in their own batches, which run as followup-deep. The owner may change any of these.

outage_desk._note: The outage desk (scripts/outage-desk.mjs): which unchecked outage reports an outage checker verifies. recheck_hours: a report (or another report with the same key, e.g. the same country's IODA signal on another day) checked this recently is not checked again, and the wait doubles with every not_confirmed check in a row on that key (12, 24, 48 h ...), never more than recheck_max_hours, unless the report is stronger than the last check saw (an IODA score or stated figure stronger_factor times as high, one more publisher, a new cyberattack headline: then at once; scripts/lib/gates.mjs outageRecheck; measured to 2026-11-23, all 34 IODA checks were not_confirmed, the same six countries twice a day); max_tries: a not_confirmed report is checked again after recheck_hours until this many tries; confirmed and cyber_lead are final. News-reported power outages (not taken by the grid desk, no operator incident open in that country): a stated figure of news_min_figure or more, news_min_publishers or more publishers, a nationwide headline or a cyber headline; a stated figure below news_skip_below is left out unless a headline speaks of a cyberattack. IODA: a country score of ioda_min_score or more, or ioda_min_signals or more independent measurements. Status pages: leads of kind status from the last status_hours. A country or provider with a category outage event in the last event_days days is already on the map. The owner may change any of these.

claims_desk._note: The claims desk (scripts/claims-desk.mjs): which leak-site claims (leads of kind claim) a claims checker verifies. window_days: claims read from the leads of this many days. new_hours: a claim never checked is taken only while it is younger than this. recheck_hours: the base wait before an unconfirmed claim is checked again; it doubles with every check in a row that gave the same result (24, 48, 96 h), never more than recheck_max_hours, until max_tries; confirmed_by_victim, reported, denied and not_found are final (the follow-up desk takes a claimed event from there). A new report that names the victim (not a leak site) brings an unconfirmed or not_found claim back at once, also after max_tries, for at most reopen_tries more checks (scripts/lib/gates.mjs claimRecheck; owner, 2026-11-23: all 189 checks so far were unconfirmed or not_found). recheck_min_score (0 = off): with a value above 0, a claim whose notability score is under it is never re-checked on the timer, only when a report names the victim. match_days: a claim whose victim is named by an incident event dated within this many days is already on the map and is left out. Masked victims (private people) are never queued. The owner may change any of these.

usage_budget._note: The Max plan has no dollar limit but a 5-hour and a weekly usage window, and it does not publish them. These are estimates (scripts/lib/usage.mjs reads data/usage/*.jsonl, headless workers only; the ops and interactive sessions use the same plan and are not counted, so keep a margin). Derived 2026-11-20 from 26.6 hours of the usage log (2026-11-19 04:35 to 11-20 07:13), no limit hit in that time: peak rolling 5 hours 86.0 M tokens and $40.05 (19 Nov 17:47 to 22:47, while two loops ran at once), x 1.5 = window_tokens and window_cost. The log holds less than a week, so the weekly figures are the peak rolling 24 hours (319.1 M tokens, $152.25) x 7 x 1.5. Levels: tight at tight_pct of either window (the loop runs only researchers on incidents and exploited flaws and reviewers past 20 minutes; the jobs in tight_skip_jobs wait), stop at stop_pct of the 5-hour window or on a real limit hit (no workers until the reset time the error gives, else limit_backoff_minutes). The weekly estimate never stops the loop by itself. Re-derive these once a full week of the log exists (node scripts/lib/usage.mjs prints the current level and the peaks). Owner, 2026-11-21: "use whatever it needs": the only protection left is the stop level. tight_cuts_work false (the default) makes tight work like ok: researchers, reviewers, updaters, grid and outage workers, the follow-up desk, gap searchers and the jobs in tight_skip_jobs all run; set it to true to restore the old tight behaviour (scripts/run-job.mjs workAt, scripts/dispatch.mjs). Re-derived 2026-11-22 (owner: fix the loop stopping for usage) from 3.6 days of the log: the 5-hour peak with no limit hit inside it is 126.1 M tokens and $74.42 (12:58 to 17:58 UTC on 22 Nov), x 1.5 = window_tokens 189 M and window_cost $112 (was 129 M / $60, which stopped the loop at $72 while no limit was near). Real 5-hour limit hits (2026-11-21 22:55, 2026-11-22 01:58 and 09:07) came at only $19 to $66 of headless spend because the ops and interactive sessions share the window and are not counted, so no headless-only estimate can predict them: the real-limit stop (a worker's limit error, until the reset time it gives) is what catches those. The weekly figures are left as they were: the 24-hour peak window includes those limit hits, and the account's 7-day limit was already at a warning, so the weekly estimate is not loosened. pipeline_reserve_pct (owner, 2026-11-23, after a code-build swarm used the whole 5-hour window on 22 November and the pipeline published nothing for 2.5 hours): this share of the 5-hour estimate is kept for the pipeline. Work that is not the pipeline (code builds, swarms) runs `node scripts/budget.mjs can-build` before it launches agents and between waves, and waits while it exits non-zero: the window above (100 - reserve)% of the estimate, or the plan refused a pipeline worker in the last hour (scripts/lib/usage.mjs canBuild). It does not change when the pipeline itself stops. A worker that hits the limit is recorded as that (ledger `limit`, `limit_until`), no further worker is started in that run, and the pipeline check reports "usage limit reached, resets <time>".

api_fallback._note: API-key fallback (owner-approved 2026-11-23; scripts/lib/usage.mjs, scripts/run-job.mjs). The Max subscription stays PRIMARY: the pipeline publishes on it and the Anthropic API bills ONLY while the subscription's 5-hour/weekly window is exhausted (a worker hit the plan's real limit; budgetState limited_until is live), so publishing never stalls. The owner stores the fallback key in the environment under the NON-standard name CYBERVIEW_FALLBACK_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (never ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, which the claude CLI would use ahead of the subscription); the normal worker env has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and only in fallback mode does run-job.mjs inject ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<that value> into the spawned worker. With the env var unset, behaviour is exactly as before (park on a limit). When the reset passes, a worker runs on the subscription again and the key is dropped automatically. Guards: enabled turns it off (then park as before); monthly_usd_cap is the ceiling on API-billed spend per calendar month (estimated from each api-fallback worker's tokens x the PRICES table in scripts/lib/usage.mjs, which the owner updates when Anthropic changes prices) — once reached the pipeline parks instead of falling back and the pipeline check raises 'API fallback monthly cap reached'; if the fallback key itself hits a usage limit the pool parks for the rest of the run instead of looping. The key VALUE is never in the repo, never logged, never printed (only process.env is read, masked to present/not-set). Telemetry: each worker's ledger line carries served subscription|api-fallback; efficiency.json gains an api_fallback block; the pipeline check reports 'running on API fallback' (info) and the cap (needs attention); scripts/budget.mjs status prints the state and the $ this month.
